summary: Round 24 recheck, 28 Sep 06:40-07:10Z. At the 06:42:35Z poll header, probes 47/48/49/50 were all PENDING and the best was still exp70g at 0.956. The 66 items rechecked in rounds 2-23 were skipped, except where a new measurement contradicts a round-23 mechanism. All three picks are on the discussion-743929 readmit/ILP line that probe 50 (exp85a) is testing. Each was measured on CPU from the downloaded dummy outputs (_dl/biohub-exp70g/85a/85b/85c) and the exp60 lab. Nothing was built, pushed, submitted or committed. (C) is the one that matters for today's slots. (C) ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT (RESULTS probe 3; R11-RC-B; R23-RC-B 'no output channel'; CONTEXT 06:26Z 'exp85b near-inert, a near-duplicate of exp70g'). This is WRONG in the fork dimension. On the dummy, ILP 0.4 adds exactly +3 SAFE divisions (63 -> 66; +1 on 3 of 4 clips, 0 on the fourth; +4.8% safe forks) for +49 net nodes. The effect adds exactly on top of READMIT 0.94 (exp85c 82 forks -> exp85a 85). The channel: the ILP keeps more daughter nodes (raw nodes +84), the 1:1 relink leaves them as orphans, and the purely geometric post-link safe-division stage pairs them. So JT's +0.001 has a real path on our stack. The path is division supply on a pool that the cap ladder does not touch, and division adds have been public-positive (probe 45). Probe 50's fork change is therefore 3 safe divisions from ILP plus 1 insertion from READMIT, together with +1,076 nodes. exp85b is the clean one-knob read of the division part. (A) C05's lowrefine '>= 0.965 only, head in distribution' restriction. READMIT_MIN_SCORE 0.94 lifts it silently, because the builder reads the lowrefine threshold from BIOHUB_READMIT_MIN_SCORE (the round-23 'two changes' alert). Measured: +4,386 extra refined pool peaks with 0 failed frames. The new band nodes carry head coordinates (8.3% sit on the 4-px grid vs 7.3% for all nodes), where JT's base leaves them on the 1.625 um grid. Lowrefine alone was display-neutral (#38 = 0.953 = x138). NEW VERDICT: the coupling is benign and second-order. exp85a/exp85c are one coherent change ('readmit band with K2 coordinates'), not two levers, and no decoupling build is needed. (B) I-183 READMIT_RADIUS_UM. It was closed with x138-tail recalibration because 'pool peaks are unrefined int16, so the premise does not apply'. That reason is void on K2, where lowrefine refines the pool. The radius was never measured. In-sample extension pools are (4,5] um 3,078 (+0.27% nodes) and (5,6] um 3,812 (+0.34%). The lab is blind to them (R23-RC-C) and there is no public anchor. It STAYS CLOSED for slots with the corrected reason, and it is not the follow-up to a '+' on probe 50.

findings.what: ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT 1.2 -> 0.4, the half of probe 50 / exp85a that came from discussion 743929. OLD VERDICTS: (1) RESULTS probe 3 (exp18, 0.9 on the 0.941 base) = 0.941, 'neutral, dropped'. (2) R11-RC-B: closed, 'no channel: x138's relink is 1:1 and emits no ILP forks'. (3) R23-RC-B: 'STAYS CLOSED, no output channel in x138 (the relink replaces all ILP edges; 0/56 raw fallbacks; appearance 0 makes an ILP fork's second child an orphan either way, so the orphan supply is essentially unchanged); JT's +0.001 is base-specific'. (4) CONTEXT 06:26Z decomposition: 'ILP 0.4 alone moves +49 nodes / +3 forks (near-inert on our base, as R23-RC-B predicted) ... exp85b is a near-duplicate of exp70g, so it buys little information'. WHAT CHANGED (measured today on the dummy run_stats.csv and submission.csv files): safe_divisions_added goes from exp70g 35/6/5/17 = 63 to exp85b 36/7/5/18 = 66, and from exp85c 63 to exp85a 66. divins_added is unchanged by ILP (6/0/6/6). READMIT 0.94 adds exactly one insertion (44b6_0b24845f 0 -> 1). Forks decompose exactly: exp70g 81 = 63 safe + 18 ins; exp85b 84 = 66 + 18; exp85c 82 = 63 + 19; exp85a 85 = 66 + 19. raw_nodes +7/+30/0/+47 (+84); motion_relink_replaced_raw_edges +832; division_like_sources +1/+1/0/+1; node churn exp70g -> exp85b: 273 new / 224 lost / 83 moved <= 1 um, identical on exp85c -> exp85a. add_safe_divisions_postlink (exp70g cell 7 l.1498-1636) is purely geometric on the POST-relink graph: sources with one child, candidates = nodes with no incoming edge, parent <= 9 um, sister <= 14 um, divergence, DeepCenter veto, symmetry tau. MECHANISM: a cheaper ILP division lets the ILP keep more daughter nodes. The 1:1 relink cannot give them a parent, so they stay orphans, and the safe-division stage pairs some of them, all past the DC veto. R23-RC-B was right that ILP forks never reach the output directly. It was wrong that the orphan supply is unchanged: the ILP decides which daughter NODES exist. The +3 is in the same direction on 3 of 4 clips and 0 on the fourth, so it is systematic, not churn noise. In size it is about half a cap step (cap 6 -> 8 = +5 forks on the dummy), and it acts on a different pool (safe divisions, not insertions), so it is not redundant with the cap ladder. NEW VERDICT: the 'no channel' reason is FALSIFIED. JT's +0.001 has a plausible path on our stack through division supply, the lever class that is public-positive for us (0.954 -> 0.956 at probe 45; the insertion +0.001 three times). The node cost is negligible (+0.04%). exp85b is NOT a near-duplicate of exp70g: it is the only clean read of a +3-safe-fork, ~0-node lever. Probe 50 bundles it with a +0.84% node-volume change (READMIT) whose public sign is split. Private caveat: safe-division precision on other embryos is unknown, and the lab has been wrong in sign for division knobs, so public reads are the only judge. Realistic public effect of exp85b: +0.000..+0.001 (P(display +1 over exp70g) ~0.25-0.35); private sign mildly positive by the division-add record, uncertain.

findings.what: v3 s_merge C05 (lowrefine = K2's 'lowrefine' patch). OLD VERDICT / DESIGN RULE: 'refine only the >= 0.965 part of x138's lowdet pool (these are exactly the ILP-discarded main peaks the head refined before the ILP, so it is in distribution); leave the 0.5-0.965 gapfill peaks on the integer grid (head out of distribution there)'. The 04:53Z curator alert turned this into 'exp85a changes TWO things: READMIT_MIN_SCORE 0.94 also sets K2's lowrefine threshold'. WHAT CHANGED: tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.1652 sets _LOWREFINE_MIN_SCORE = float(os.environ.get('BIOHUB_READMIT_MIN_SCORE', '0.965')), so every READMIT rung (exp85a/85c/86a/86b/86c) also moves the refinement boundary. MEASURED on the dummy logs: refined pool peaks exp70g 26,532/33,336/7,370/76,396 -> exp85c 26,694/36,487/7,497/77,342 (+4,386; of 27,877/51,793/8,518/81,321 pool peaks), failed frames 0 on every clip. Readmits 96/677/84/508 = 1,365 -> 167/1,148/105/804 = 2,224. Unrefined pool rows sit on the pooled grid multiplied by downsample (4 px = 1.625 um in xy). In the exp85c CSV, 154 of the 1,857 new nodes (> 1 um from any exp70g node) lie on the 4-px xy grid = 8.3%, against 7.3% for all exp70g nodes and 6.25% at random, so the band readmits carry head coordinates. JT's base has no lowrefine, so his band readmits stay on the grid. Lowrefine on the >= 0.965 pool was display-neutral (#38 = x138 + safetail + lowrefine = 0.953 = #34). Peaks at 0.94-0.965 are the same detector maxima, with the same feature map and the same head input, just below the main cutoff. The out-of-distribution concern in C05 was about gapfill-level peaks (0.5), which stay unrefined. Side fact: exp85c against exp70g churns 1,857 new / 835 lost / 1,056 moved <= 1 um nodes for +1,022 net, so READMIT reshapes the second relink and the later stages; it is not a pure add. NEW VERDICT: C05's rule is sound for gapfill-level scores. At 0.94, and at 0.92 for exp86c, the coupling is benign and second-order: sub-voxel moves under a 7 um match radius, in the direction of better localisation. exp85a/exp85c are ONE coherent change ('readmit band with K2 coordinates'), not a hidden second lever. Read probe 50 and exp85c as node-volume reads. No decoupling build (a separate BIOHUB_LOWREFINE_MIN_SCORE) is warranted; it would only put the band readmits back on the coarse grid. Do not use 'two changes' as an attribution excuse for a '-' on 50.

findings.what: I-183: the readmit-radius part of v3's 'x138-tail recalibration for refined coords' (C06; READMIT_RADIUS_UM 4, grid 3/4/5). OLD VERDICT: refuted together with the linefit w0.7 arm. The only measured arm was linefit (exp60: 44b6 -0.0031, 6bba +0.0001; R6-RC-C: null). The radius was never measured. It was dismissed by the value skeptic because 'readmit/gapfill peaks come from the lowdet dump = UNREFINED int16 -> the refined-coords premise does not apply; the radius changes the node count (multiplier artefact)'. The public stage chain was 'flow2 0.947 -> +gapfill 0.947 -> +readmit 0.946'. WHAT CHANGED: (1) K2's lowrefine refines the pool rows >= READMIT_MIN_SCORE, so on our base the readmit candidates ARE refined and the recorded reason is void. (2) JT's step shows that the readmit stage can move public (+0.001 at 0.94), and probe 50 tests it. (3) R23-RC-C: the lab is blind to sub-threshold/readmit node value. MEASURED (exp60 lab, 56 clips; score >= 0.965; free peaks > 2 um from presafe nodes; distance to the nearest open end/start anchor): (0,4] 4,325 (17 within 4 um of GT); (4,5] 3,078 = +0.27% of 1,124,511 final nodes (13 near GT; 44b6 1,174, 6bba 1,904); (5,6] 3,812 = +0.34% (27 near GT; 44b6 1,471, 6bba 2,341). These are in-sample counts of the node cost only; the recall side is invisible, as for READMIT_MIN_SCORE. NEW VERDICT: the reason is corrected ('never measured; lab-blind'), but the idea STAYS CLOSED for 28-29 Sep slots. It has no public anchor, unlike JT's two knobs. It is our own knob rung, banned in W3/W4 by W4 AMEND 2 (4). A 4 -> 5 um radius reaches farther from the open end, where neighbouring nuclei (~7-10 um spacing in 6bba) start to compete, so its precision prior is lower than the 0.94 band's. It is NOT the follow-up to a '+' on probe 50. That follow-up stays in the disclosed direction (exp86c READMIT 0.92, already built), and exp86c's in-sample band [0.90, 0.94) is +0.43% nodes (R23). Post-deadline: test radius and threshold together on an embryo-held-out bed or with late submissions.
